hard_gate_findings.evidence: Gating harness check run.argv_invalid_utf8 (K8) fails deterministically. Invalid-UTF-8 argv is silently rewritten to U+FFFD with exit 0. This is a stack limitation under K8. Further defects of the K6 mechanism, beyond the harness: (1) when proto shares the foreground job with another process that reads the tty, it hands the terminal to the child's group, so 'heimdall-proto run -- <long cmd> | less' in bash -i is Stopped (env control completes; non-interactive sh gives EIO); (2) inherited SIG_IGN dispositions are reset for the child, and nohup-style HUP kills it (rc 129 vs 0 direct); (3) a process-group SIGKILL orphans the child; (4) RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit is raised (256 to 1048576) for the child. Agent IPC passed all crafted bound tests; one nondeterminism remains (trailing bytes after a complete frame). Stdio, EOF, backpressure, exit statuses and signal races were all correct.

Code review only - not native evidence. windows-x64 PE plus opentui.dll builds. run uses Bun.spawn with windowsVerbatimArguments and a CommandLineToArgvW quoter (unit-tested against a reference decoder only). It refuses .bat/.cmd, does not forward console Ctrl-C, and relies on Bun internals for argv0 as the command-line token. The named pipe goes through node:net, with no native run. Whether exit codes above 255 and console close behave correctly is unknown. WSL: the glibc Linux build would need a glibc distro (fails on musl Alpine, observed in a container). No Windows host was available.

The artifact trusts inherited environment for code loading and file writes. BUN_OPTIONS=--preload runs arbitrary JS (macOS and Linux). BUN_INSPECT opens an inspector listener. BUN_BE_BUN gives a full runtime. OTUI_STDIN_LOG logs keystrokes (including typed text) to any path. OTUI_DEBUG_FFI writes logs to cwd. A test-only HEIMDALL_PROTO_FAULT hook ships in the artifact. BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_INSPECT are handled by the runtime before user code, so the program likely cannot scrub them (inference). Unlike DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES they would survive a hardened-runtime signed build (inference, not tested). No shell use was found. Agent lengths are bounded before allocation. Profile size is checked by fstat on an open fd (no stat-then-open TOCTOU), but a FIFO path blocks forever.

Works relocated, without a toolchain, from spaced/Unicode paths on macOS and debian arm64 (linux-x64 only emulated, by the producer). It requires the @opentui sidecar subdirectory, glibc (not musl), and 73–97 MB per target (28–42 MB gzip). The macOS build is ad-hoc signed and spctl rejects it. Hardened-runtime signing and notarization with Bun's JIT plus a dlopen'd sidecar were not tested (no Developer ID). No license or notice files ship in dist. Cross-target runtime downloads are verified only by TLS (producer claim, not checked).

Registry checked 2026-10-03: @opentui/core 0.5.14 (latest, 2026-09-30), smol-toml 1.9.0 (latest), Bun 1.4.2 (latest release 2026-09-05), bun-ffi-structs 0.3.1 (latest). All are actively released. Risk: OpenTUI is pre-1.0 with 335 versions since 2025-08 and 54 since 2026-07-01, and its native ABI is documented as internal. OpenTUI also inlines older marked 17.0.1 and string-width 7.2.0.

The npm tree is permissive (MIT/BSD-3/Apache-2.0). Every artifact statically embeds Bun's LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore/WebCore and LGPL-2.1 tinycc, which carries relink and notice obligations. The project license is undecided. dist ships no notices: 0 license/notice files found, although libwebp PATENTS, Wuffs Apache-2.0 and the Bun notices are needed. Tree-sitter grammar licenses are unchecked (per LICENSES.md). No legal review.

hard_gate_findings.gate: Ability to share domain operations across CLI/TUI
hard_gate_findings.evidence: Code review: src/domain/* is pure, and the tui command reuses readBounded + parseProfile from profile show. Selection, filter and layout live in domain/listview.ts and are unit-tested without a terminal. The OpenTUI adapter (src/tui/tui.ts) only maps keys and draws. The harness's 20+ tui.* checks and the CLI checks pass against the same build.

defects.description: K8 gating failure: argv elements that are not valid UTF-8 reach the child with every invalid byte replaced by EF BF BD, with exit 0 and no diagnostic. This is silent data corruption, deterministic, and occurs on macOS and Linux. The embedded Bun runtime decodes argv before user code. K8 rules that the FFI route counts as routing around, so the candidate cannot pass the common slice as built.
defects.location: Bun 1.4.2 runtime argv handling; src/main.ts (process.argv); harness check run.argv_invalid_utf8

defects.description: K6 terminal hand-off steals the terminal from other members of proto's foreground job. Under bash -i, 'heimdall-proto run -- sh -c "printf line1; sleep 2" | less' is Stopped (SIGTTIN). The same pipeline with /usr/bin/env completes. Under non-interactive sh, a pipeline peer reading /dev/tty gets EIO. foregroundTtyFd only checks that proto's pgrp is in the foreground, not that proto is alone in it. The outcome is race-dependent: it does not occur when the child exits immediately.
defects.location: src/platform/run.ts runChild (giveTerminal), src/platform/posix-spawn.ts foregroundTtyFd/giveTerminal; probes/out/less_bash_i_proto.log, pipeline_tty_bash_i_proto.log

defects.description: Inherited environment variables change program identity and load code. BUN_OPTIONS='--preload <file>' runs arbitrary JS before main. BUN_INSPECT opens a Bun inspector TCP listener (observed on 127.0.0.1; that listener accepts debugger connections, inference). BUN_BE_BUN=1 makes the artifact a full Bun runtime. REPORT discloses only BUN_BE_BUN. These are processed by the runtime before user code, so the program likely cannot neutralize them (inference).

Other OTUI_* or OPENTUI_* variables in the bundle (OTUI_TREE_SITTER_WORKER_PATH, OTUI_OVERRIDE_STDOUT, OTUI_USE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN, OTUI_NO_NATIVE_RENDER and others) were not probed.
defects.location: src/cli.ts pinNativeAssets; node_modules/@opentui/core chunk-bun-j2z63cdy.js:7333/9065 (stdinLogPath), chunk-bun-sjw2d9bq.js:15413-15440 (FFI debug log); probes/out/otui_env.log

defects.description: TUI selected row is styled fg #ffffff on bg #ffffff with SGR 7 (reverse) and bold. OpenTUI already swaps the colors and then also emits reverse. With fg == bg the selected row, including its '> ' marker, is likely invisible on truecolor terminals (inference from SGR semantics; observed only through pyte cell attributes). Unselected rows use hard-coded fg #ffffff and would be invisible on light-background terminals (inference). The harness checks text, not legibility.

defects.description: Signal dispositions are not inherited like exec. SETSIGDEF with a full set resets SIG_IGN dispositions inherited from proto's parent (nohup, non-interactive background jobs) to default. proto also installs a HUP handler over an inherited SIG_IGN. Result: 'trap "" HUP; heimdall-proto run -- sleep 2 &' dies on HUP (rc 129); the direct command survives (rc 0). On Linux the child also starts with signals 32 and 33 ignored (SigIgn 0x180000000).
defects.location: src/platform/posix-spawn.ts spawnInOwnGroup (SETSIGDEF with sigfillset); src/platform/run.ts FORWARDED handlers; probes/out/nohup_hup.log, sigign_rlimit.log

defects.description: Bun raises the RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit at startup and the child inherits it (256 becomes 1048576 on macOS and Linux). This silently changes the child's resource limits.
defects.location: Bun runtime startup; probes/out/sigign_rlimit.log, linux probe

defects.description: Because the child runs in its own process group, a process-group SIGKILL of proto's group (CI cancellation, supervisors) orphans the child. A plain wrapper's child dies with the group. REPORT's K6 gap list mentions only terminal ownership on SIGKILL.

agent list depends on segmentation. Trailing bytes after a complete valid frame give AGENT_PROTOCOL_ERROR when they arrive in the same read and AGENT_OK when they arrive in a later read. Identical byte streams can yield different results.

summary:
I rebuilt independently in /tmp/hm-review-root/prototypes/ts (symlinked from /tmp/heimdall-review-ts). All four executables and sidecars are byte-identical to the measured dist (darwin-arm64 dd7a771d…). My own full harness run reproduces the recorded verdict: harness exit 1, 112/113 pass, 0 errors. The only failure is the gating K8 check run.argv_invalid_utf8. Using the artifact's embedded Bun (BUN_BE_BUN -e), I confirmed the cause: Bun decodes argv to U+FFFD before user code runs, so non-UTF-8 argv is silently corrupted with exit 0. This blocks the common slice.

The producer's own suite passes 154/154 from source and against the artifact. It first failed (7 errors) because I ran it outside the repo layout; that was my error, and those logs are kept.

Probes beyond the harness confirmed these as sound:
- stdin EOF propagation, backpressure with large stdout and stderr, binary bytes, environment bytes and cwd.
- Exit and signal statuses: 153/153 correct on macOS and on Linux arm64.
- Signal startup races: no lost or duplicate deliveries.
- All 20 crafted agent frames hit their bounds correctly.
- CLI and TUI share their domain operations.

The probes also found defects the harness does not cover:
1. **Pipelines that read the terminal break.** The K6 terminal hand-off takes the terminal away from other processes in the same foreground job. Under bash -i, `heimdall-proto run -- <long cmd> | less` ends up Stopped.
2. **Environment variables load code or open a listener.** BUN_OPTIONS=--preload runs arbitrary JS. BUN_INSPECT silently opens an inspector listener (observed on 127.0.0.1). REPORT mentions neither; it covers only BUN_BE_BUN.
3. **Writes outside named paths.** With OTUI_STDIN_LOG set, the TUI writes every keystroke, including typed text, to a file the environment chooses. With OTUI_DEBUG_FFI set, it writes logs into the working directory. This refutes the K11 "no writes outside named paths" claim in the general case.
4. **Selected row likely unreadable.** It is drawn white on white with reverse video. I saw this only through the pyte terminal emulator's cell attributes; that it is invisible on a real terminal is my inference.
5. **Minor child-transparency gaps:**
   - Ignored signals inherited from the parent are reset, so nohup-style use dies on HUP.
   - Signals 32 and 33 are ignored in the child on Linux.
   - The open-file soft limit is raised (256 to 1048576).
   - A process-group SIGKILL leaves the child orphaned.
6. **Smaller items:**
   - Trailing agent bytes are classified differently depending on how the reads are split.
   - A profile path that is a FIFO with no writer hangs.
   - revision above 2^53-1 is rejected; the contract is ambiguous here and needs a ruling, not a decision from me.
   - A test-only fault hook ships in the artifact.
   - REPORT has stale Linux and Windows hashes.

Gate verdicts:

| Gate | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Child/IPC correctness | fail |
| No unsupported security assumption | fail |
| Windows/WSL viability | uncertain (code review only - not native evidence) |
| Practical distribution | uncertain (glibc-only, 73–97 MB, ad-hoc signed, no notices in dist) |
| Licensing | uncertain (static LGPL JavaScriptCore, project license undecided) |
| Maintained dependencies | pass (pre-1.0 OpenTUI with heavy churn) |
| Shared CLI/TUI domain operations | pass |

All evidence is in tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-ts/review/: harness/, selftests/, probes/scripts and probes/out (including run_all.sh with per-probe exit codes), build.log and review-build-manifest.json. I made no writes outside that directory and /tmp. The measured repo artifact is unchanged (sha256 dd7a771d…). Two side effects:
- My `docker run --platform linux/arm64 debian:trixie` pulled the arm64 image (manifest digest 9cc08002…). The local tag debian:trixie now resolves to the arm64 image sha256:22bcbd63… instead of the earlier 36c636ddb9c5. Other agents using that tag without --platform may be affected.
- I briefly opened a loopback-only inspector listener on 127.0.0.1:47391 during the BUN_INSPECT probe.

No processes were left running.
